stretch.name: STRETCH
stretch.oneLiner: The company the group grew out of: Belgian maker of seamless polyester stretch ceilings and walls, produced in-house, sold through dealers and installed in one day.
stretch.whatTitle: A new ceiling in one day.
stretch.description: STRETCH designs and makes seamless stretch ceilings and walls in Beveren-Waas, Belgium. The polyester membrane is mounted cold and installed in a single day, with acoustic, lighting and printed options. Michael Nicasens founded the company in 2018 (Stretch Productions BV) with one goal: a stretch-ceiling brand that produces its own system and promotes and sells it through a worldwide dealer network, so that existing interior businesses can add a product with real margin. Production is heavily automated — STRETCH built its own roll-handling machine that cuts every ceiling automatically. Belgium is served from stretchplafond.be, international markets from stretch.mt.
bullets: Seamless polyester stretch ceilings and walls
Cold-mounted, installed in one day
Acoustic, lighting and printed options
Produced in-house on its own automated cutting line
Sold through a dealer network: stretchplafond.be (BE) · stretch.mt (international)
stretch.ctaBody: Products, projects, prices and quotes live on the STRETCH website.

stretch-sufit.name: Stretch Sufit
stretch-sufit.oneLiner: PVC stretch-ceiling factory in Częstochowa, Poland, producing since 2016 — bought by STRETCH in 2024 as the group’s base for Eastern Europe.
stretch-sufit.description: Alto Design Sp. z o.o. has produced PVC stretch ceilings in Częstochowa since 2016, seamless up to 6.50 m. STRETCH bought the factory in 2024: it produces at roughly a third of the Belgian production cost, gave the group a strong boost and opened the Eastern European market. Its consumer installation brand, Stretch Sufit, is active in 17 Polish cities and has completed more than 4,000 projects.
bullets: PVC stretch-ceiling factory in Częstochowa since 2016
Seamless PVC up to 6.50 m
Bought by STRETCH in 2024 — the group’s gateway to Eastern Europe
Stretch Sufit: installation in 17 Polish cities
More than 4,000 completed projects
stretch-sufit.ctaBody: Quotes, installations and the factory range live on altodesign.pl.

re-sound.name: Re-Sound
re-sound.oneLiner: Belgian producer of circular acoustic panels and screens from recycled and sustainable materials — part of STRETCH Group since the end of 2025.
re-sound.description: Re-Sound makes acoustic panels and screens in Belgium from recycled and sustainable materials. It started in 2020 with yarn spun from recycled jeans. Every product can be returned at the end of its life and made into new panels. The range includes Interior panels and the Divide freestanding screen. Founded by Aaron Thierens, Re-Sound was acquired by STRETCH Group at the end of 2025 to broaden the group’s range into acoustic panels.
bullets: Acoustic panels and screens made in Belgium
Recycled and sustainable materials, starting from recycled jeans yarn in 2020
Full take-back policy: close the loop
Interior panels and the Divide freestanding screen
Part of STRETCH Group since the end of 2025
re-sound.ctaBody: The range, projects and contact for acoustic solutions live on re-sound.be.

stretch-metal.name: Stretch Metal
stretch-metal.oneLiner: The group’s own metal workshop, opened in 2026: structures in every kind of metal, from metal ceilings and balustrades to hall structures and stainless-steel kitchen elements.
stretch-metal.whatTitle: Every kind of metal, every kind of project.
stretch-metal.description: Stretch Metal started out of necessity: the group needed metal fabrication for its own prefab elements and for the large structures its projects require. As that work scaled it took on jobs for other companies too, and in 2026 the group opened its own metal workshop under the Stretch Metal name. It builds structures in every kind of metal for every kind of project — the metal ceilings at Spa-Francorchamps, balustrades, hall structures, generator panels and stainless-steel kitchen elements.
bullets: Metal ceilings, including at Spa-Francorchamps
Balustrades and hall structures
Generator panels and stainless-steel kitchen elements
Prefab elements for the group, fabrication jobs for other companies
Own workshop, opened in 2026

hero.lead: STRETCH Group grew out of one Belgian stretch-ceiling company into four: a stretch-ceiling maker in Belgium, a PVC factory in Poland, a circular-acoustics producer in Belgium and a metal workshop. Each keeps its own name and website; the group connects them.

story.title: From one company to four.
story.p1: STRETCH Group grew out of one company. In 2018 Michael Nicasens founded STRETCH in Beveren-Waas, Belgium, with a clear goal: build a stretch-ceiling brand that produces its own system and promotes and sells it through a worldwide dealer network — so that existing interior businesses can add a product with real margin. The first sales employee joined at the end of that year; the first admin and warehouse colleagues followed in 2019.
story.p2: From the start the company invested heavily in automation, building its own roll-handling machine that cuts every stretch ceiling automatically and makes the work safer. When COVID hit in 2020, STRETCH kept investing and growing. A Belgian PVC production unit, opened in 2021, proved financially too heavy and was later stopped; the Austrian sales office, opened in 2022, had a tough start and is paying off today.
story.p3: In 2024 STRETCH bought Alto Design, a PVC stretch-ceiling factory in Częstochowa, Poland, producing at roughly a third of the Belgian cost. It gave STRETCH a strong boost and opened the Eastern European market. At the end of 2025 Re-Sound, a Belgian producer of acoustic panels, joined to broaden the range into acoustics. In 2026 the group opened its own metal workshop, Stretch Metal: structures in every kind of metal, from the metal ceilings at Spa-Francorchamps to balustrades, hall structures, generator panels and stainless-steel kitchen elements.
story.p4: The goal for 2027 is to use the synergies of the four companies through the existing dealer network: become more densely present in the markets the group already serves, and grow the footprint from there. Each company keeps its own brand and website:

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This privacy policy explains how STRETCH Group (“we”, “us”) collects and uses personal data when you visit stretchgroup.be or contact us through it. We are the data controller for that processing.

p: We only collect what we need. When you use the contact form or send an open application, we collect the details you provide: your name, email address, company, which company your message concerns, and the contents of your message.

When you browse the site we may also collect standard technical and usage data — such as device, browser and pages viewed — through cookies and similar technologies, but only to the extent you have consented. You can review and change your choices at any time via “Manage cookies” in the footer.

We use the details you submit to answer your enquiry and to forward it to the group company that can help you (STRETCH, Stretch Sufit / Alto Design or Re-Sound). This processing is based on your request and our legitimate interest in responding to it.
Where you have given consent, we use analytics technologies to understand how the site is used and to improve it. You may withdraw consent at any time.

Google Analytics is loaded with Google Consent Mode set to “denied” by default: until you accept analytics it sets no cookies, stores no identifiers and only sends cookieless, aggregated signals. Microsoft Clarity is only loaded after you accept analytics. Essential cookies needed to operate the site and to remember your cookie choice do not require consent.

To protect our forms against automated abuse we may use Cloudflare Turnstile, a privacy-preserving verification service provided by Cloudflare, Inc. It evaluates technical signals from your browser to tell people apart from bots and does not track you across sites. We also record technical details of form submissions, such as IP address and browser type, for the same purpose. This processing is based on our legitimate interest in keeping the site secure.

We do not sell your personal data. We share it with the group company your enquiry concerns, and with service providers who help us operate the site and deliver messages — our hosting provider, our email provider and, where consented, our analytics providers — only as needed to perform those services. Some providers may process data outside the European Economic Area; in that case appropriate safeguards apply.

We keep enquiry data for as long as needed to handle your request and for our legitimate business and legal record-keeping, after which it is deleted or anonymised. Open applications are kept for a limited period unless you ask us to delete them earlier.

Subject to applicable law, you have the right to access, correct, delete or restrict the processing of your personal data, to object to processing, to data portability, and to withdraw consent at any time. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority. In Belgium this is the Data Protection Authority (Gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit).
